citations.F1: N+1 query: `serialize_event` does a per-row `SELECT ... FROM users` — for 1000 events that's 1000 round trips. Batch with one `WHERE id = ANY($1)` or a join.
citations.F2: O(n²) dedupe: ... Python dedupes with `if ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` (list scan)
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get` inside an `async def` handler, blocking the whole event loop
citations.F4: no index on `events(org_id, created_at)` — Postgres is scanning/sorting against 4.2M rows for every call
citations.F5: `_request_timings` is also appended to forever and never trimmed — bound it (ring buffer or reservoir)
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict that never evicts ... Bound it (LRU/TTL/max size).
citations.F7: After 2–7 land, re-measure p50/p95 for acme and northwind before deciding whether workers/pool size need to move at all.
citations.F9: On-call's worker/pool bump: reject — 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 DB connections ... only add it once the endpoint itself is fast
citations.F11: `since` defaults to `datetime.now(timezone.utc) - 30d` computed fresh per request, so the cache key is different on almost every call and will essentially never hit
